lines: Dr. Mark Hyman, co-founder of Function Health, argues longevity comes from the compounding effect of small daily habits in strength, nutrition, sleep and stress, not from extreme one-off interventions.
He calls muscle mass the core currency of aging well and says people over 60 need 1.5 to 2 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight, favoring animal protein for its higher leucine content.

He warns that GLP-1 weight-loss drugs risk serious muscle loss unless paired with high protein intake and strength training, and blames frequent snacking for metabolic syndrome, urging a return to structured meals.
Hyman sees preventive medicine shifting to cheap, large-scale data such as genomics, advanced blood panels, imaging and AI analysis to catch imbalances decades before symptoms appear.

He also urges cutting exposure to environmental toxins and microplastics and claims modern hybridized wheat is more inflammatory; peptides and supplements, in his view, only help on top of the basics.
title: Mark Hyman’s Guide to Living Longer and Staying Strong
